title: Controllers, Ownership and Change of Control
summary: How to assess proposed controllers at authorisation and on a change of control, trace beneficial ownership through complex structures, and keep unsuitable owners out of the sector.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to assess proposed controllers at authorisation and on a change of control, trace beneficial ownership through complex structures, and keep unsuitable owners out of the sector.
Learning Objectives: Explain what triggers a change-of-control assessment and the criteria applied
Trace beneficial ownership through layered or opaque structures
Formulate an outcome on a proposed change of control
Syllabus: Notifiable changes of control, timelines and procedure
Assessing a proposed controller: reputation, financial soundness, plans
Trusts, nominees and layered structures as risk indicators
Exercise: tracing ownership through a sample structure
Intended Audience: Authorisation, licensing and registration staff assessing new applications and changes to existing firms
Fitness and propriety and governance specialists assessing controllers, directors and senior managers
Supervisors and financial crime specialists who contribute to authorisation decisions or take over newly authorised firms
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of authorisation, supervision or financial crime work is helpful. No legal or accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
IAIS, Insurance Core Principles and Common Framework for the Supervision of Internationally Active Insurance Groups (ComFrame)
FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
